title: Derived extension-by-zero and restriction adjunction
statement: Let (X, O_X) be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], let j:U \to X be an open inclusion, and let j_! be the exact extension-by-zero functor left adjoint to restriction on sheaves of O-modules [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact]. Applying these exact functors termwise to complexes gives functors on the derived categories D(O_U) and D(O_X) of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every A in D(O_U) and B in D(O_X) there is a natural bijection Hom_{D(O_X)}(j_! A, B) = Hom_{D(O_U)}(A, B restricted to U).

source.place: Tag 08BW proof, using Tags 08BS and 08BT (derived extension-by-zero/restriction adjunction)

proof.text: Set $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_U)$, with $F=j^{-1}:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G=j_!:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$. Both functors are exact and additive by [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact], and $G$ is left adjoint to $F$ there. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to each of $F$ and $G$ gives functors on the derived categories whose values are represented by applying the corresponding functor termwise to any complex; the same statement says that the termwise functors carry quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Hence for a complex $K$ of $\mathcal A$ every transition map of the ind-system $(F(K'))_{K\to K'}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal B)$, so the system is essentially constant with value $F(K)$; dually for the pro-system $(G(M'))_{M'\to M}$. Thus $RF$ and $LG$ in the sense of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] are defined at every complex and are computed termwise.

source.place: Lemma 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), parts (2)-(4), applied to the exact functors j_! and j^{-1}

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] now hold for the adjoint pair $G=j_!\dashv F=j^{-1}$: the module categories are abelian, their derived categories are [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the left and right derived functors are defined everywhere by Step 1. The lemma therefore gives a canonical bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(j_!A,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(A,j^{-1}B)$, functorial in $A$ and $B$. Since the derived restriction is represented termwise by restriction, this is the asserted restriction of $B$ to $U$.
